newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia leader steps up courtship of rebels.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia leader steps up courtship of rebels.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen has stepped up the courtship of breakaway Khmer Rouge rebels this week, offering their leader terms which could help cement his ties with this resource-rich region, analysts said.

But while Hun Sen may have smoothed his own relations with breakaway leader Ieng Sary, another rift remained -- that between Ieng Sary and Khmer Rouge who have defected directly to the government, analysts said.
"There is more to this than meets the eye," said one Western analyst. "There are personal problems causing antagonism."
Khmer Rouge dissidents told Reuters they were furious over the negotiating role of Keo Pong, a former Khmer Rouge with the rank of general in the coalition government.

Keo Pong, who defected earlier this year, has become the point man for Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party in talks with the Khmer Rouge. He recently helped bring over thousands of Khmer Rouge defectors directly to the government.
Bitter Khmer Rouge dissidents say some of the defectors had intended to join Ieng Sary's faction, which broke with hardliners in August but has yet to join government forces.
"Keo Pong is greedy, he is a traitor," said one battalion commander.
Long Norin, an adviser to Ieng Sary, also expressed anger over what he viewed as Keo Pong's bypassing of the dissident faction to recruit directly to the government.
The Western analyst said Keo Pong and Ei Chien, commander of Pailin, maintain a sharp rivalry over who can gather up the most troops for their side.
Ei Chien is eager to add to the Ieng Sary breakaway faction to increase its bargaining position with the government, analysts said.
In a speech during Hun Sen's visit, Ei Chien took care to address the issue of defections, noting that some wanted to proceed with integration hastily and others cautiously.
"All of us, especially at the grass-roots level, feel very worried about that," he said.

Hun Sen sought to address those worries with a visit this week to Pailin where he met with Ieng Sary, foreign minister under the 1975-79 Khmer Rouge regime of Pol Pot which caused the deaths of one million Cambodians.

The co-premier said he promised Ieng Sary new roads, schools, renovations to the Pailin temple and passports for him and his wife. Hun Sen also delivered diplomatic passports for Khmer Rouge commanders Ei Chien and Sok Peap.
In a speech before more than 3,000 villagers, Hun Sen assured the people of Pailin they would keep their gem- and timber-rich land and weapons after the area comes under government control.
Analysts said the concessions were generous and designed to overcome Ieng Sary's concern over recent defections and hesitation over putting his territory and troops under government control.

"Hun Sen is trying to indicate there is nothing to be afraid of," said the Western analyst. "He seemed to be saying...I'll give you what you want and (the issue of integration of troops) can be worked out in time."
